_rules: Every leaf is an object with value, kind and source. A leaf with no source is a bug.
kind=constant: fixed by a named party, not run-dependent.
kind=input: expected to be supplied or derived from a measurement before use.
kind=deliberately-absent: a threshold that a named party ruled must NOT exist. Emit the number, do not judge it.
kind=rejected: a value that appears in an upstream document and has been overruled. Never read it.
value=null means there is no default. The code raises at the point of use and the instrument reports COULD_NOT_BE_CHECKED_MECHANICALLY. It does not invent a number.

recompilation_events_allowed_in_window.note: A run that recompiles in-window is VOID, not adjusted. There is no adjusted path in this package.

required_env.note: Recorded into the warm-up evidence of every window so a third party can see it was set.

recompilation_event_log_patterns.source: INSTRUMENT BINDING, NOT A THRESHOLD. Must be confirmed against a real server log before first use.
recompilation_event_log_patterns.note: Regexes that identify one recompilation event in the server log. Unconfirmed: no log from a warmed v7x pod has been read by the author of this file. Until supplied, and absent an in-process counter, M0 reports COULD_NOT_BE_CHECKED_MECHANICALLY rather than zero events.

min_replicates.source: optimization-design.md section 7, M2 (>= 4 replicates, matching the H200 arm)
min_replicates.note: Extended to c1 by review-1 (pinned blob e2b63034eb5df63de7fe53456f4c6b246cbb313d) section 4.2, finding B8.

cells.source: optimization-design.md section 7 M2 (c32); review-1 section 4.2 finding B8 (c1)

serving_stack_cost_threshold_ms.source: review-1 section 4.2, finding B8: the design's 1 ms threshold VIOLATES M2's own rule and is refused.
serving_stack_cost_threshold_ms.note: Must be supplied from M2's measured spread at the same cell. There is no default and the developer did not invent one. Absent it, M3 emits the difference as an intermediate and reports COULD_NOT_BE_CHECKED_MECHANICALLY.

design_stated_threshold_ms.source: optimization-design.md section 7 M3 stated 1 ms; overruled by review-1 finding B8
design_stated_threshold_ms.note: Recorded for traceability only. Held at null so that no code path can read it.

e32_reference.source: optimization-design.md section 7, M4 (byte model stands if E(32) is within 10% of 183)
e32_reference.note: PROVENANCE FLAG, ESCALATED AND NOT ACTED ON. 183 reproduces MODEL B -- the WRONG uniform model, with replacement -- at 32 rows to three digits (182.83). MODEL A, the correct one, gives 184.47. IF this reference were re-pointed at model A, THEN the pass band would move by about 0.9% of itself and no realistic measurement would change disposition -- that is a SENSITIVITY, NOT A MEASUREMENT. It is NOT re-pointed here: the constant is the architect's to move and the question is routed to laguna-tpu-opt-arch-2. A further question is routed with it: whether the objection that retired the c1 anchor -- model output standing in for a measurement, and a ceiling rather than a centre -- also reaches this leg, which puts a SYMMETRIC 10% band around a ceiling one ladder point over.

e1_disperse_reference.source: RETIRED FROM THE DECISION PATH by the architect, 2026-08-28 17:07Z, ruled as DECIDED AND NOT AS AN ABSTENTION. Two reasons, and NEITHER IS FIXED BY A BETTER MODEL: (1) it is a MODEL OUTPUT STANDING IN FOR A MEASUREMENT, and the model it comes from carries the exact uniform-routing assumption M4 exists to test; (2) it is a CEILING, NOT A CENTRE -- any correlation between rows puts the true value below it, with no lower limit short of top-k -- so a symmetric band around it is WRONG IN FORM, not merely in width. DO NOT RE-POINT THIS AT 120.68. OPT-1850 established that 119.14 came from the wrong uniform model and that the correct model gives 120.68; OPT-1860 established that this makes the anchor MORE dangerous, not less, because a correct number reads as safe to reinstate. The retirement was never about the value being wrong. It was about the quantity being MODELLED AT ALL. The replacement rule is structural: cut = top_k_runtime + n_shared_counted, with no tolerance in it anywhere.
e1_disperse_reference.note: Left PRESENT with a null value rather than deleted, deliberately. A retired quantity left as an ABSENCE is a retired quantity waiting to be re-derived: a hole is what a future reader fills with the better number. Thresholds.require() raises on null, so any code that reaches for this anchor dies loudly instead of receiving a plausible float.

top_k_expected.source: INHERITED from laguna-tpu-opt-arch, received as bench-campaign/evidence/opt/em-succession.md at commit 64a3e599 section 4. Cited to that document per the citation rule; the sources it names were NOT opened or re-derived here. The checkpoint's own config.json gives num_experts_per_tok = 10, authoritative, corroborated by four independent load-time readings.
top_k_expected.note: ASSERTED, NOT USED AS A FALLBACK. The runtime reading is what forms the cut; this value is what the runtime reading is checked against. If top-k cannot be read from the running model the answer is UNDETERMINED, never this number.

value.8: the vLLM config-class default -- THE SERVING STACK'S OWN FALLBACK. A clean, non-dispersing system measures 8, lands below the cut and is filed as INSTRUMENT FAULT: a correct result routed into the do-not-classify bucket.
value.16: the HF default. A clean, non-dispersing system measures 16, lands above the cut and reports DISPERSAL CONFIRMED.

top_k_known_wrong_values.source: INHERITED from laguna-tpu-opt-arch, received as bench-campaign/evidence/opt/em-succession.md at commit 64a3e599 section 4. Cited to that document per the citation rule; the sources it names were NOT opened or re-derived here.
top_k_known_wrong_values.note: Both wrong values are reachable BY READING A REAL FILE IN A REAL DIRECTORY, which is why the reading must come from the running model's effective config and why a reading that parses cleanly is not thereby a reading of what the model used.

shared_experts_per_moe_layer.source: INHERITED from laguna-tpu-opt-arch, received as bench-campaign/evidence/opt/em-succession.md at commit 64a3e599 section 4. Cited to that document per the citation rule; the sources it names were NOT opened or re-derived here. One shared expert per MoE layer, always on, outside the router as a separate dense matmul.
shared_experts_per_moe_layer.note: This value does NOT decide n_shared_counted. Whether the shared expert lands in the count is a fact about WHERE THE PROBE IS, not about the model: routed GMM/Megablox rows only -> 0; experts whose weights were read -> 1. The counter declares which.

moe_layer_count.source: INHERITED from laguna-tpu-opt-arch, received as bench-campaign/evidence/opt/em-succession.md at commit 64a3e599 section 4. Cited to that document per the citation rule; the sources it names were NOT opened or re-derived here. 47 layers carry shared-expert weights, exactly the MoE layers.
moe_layer_count.note: Inherited and NOT audited here. A capture covering a different number of layers is reported UNDETERMINED rather than FAILED, because this module cannot tell a probe that missed layers from an inherited count that is wrong.

window_steps_required.source: INHERITED from laguna-tpu-opt-arch, received as bench-campaign/evidence/opt/em-succession.md at commit 64a3e599 section 4. Cited to that document per the citation rule; the sources it names were NOT opened or re-derived here. Per-step, never pooled (architect, hard).
window_steps_required.note: Not a tuning parameter and not a tolerance. A count unioned over S steps is a DIFFERENT QUANTITY, not a noisy per-step count: it rises with S and crosses the cut with certainty, and the downstream statistic is NON-MONOTONIC in S, so two honest runs at different window lengths return different answers with no disagreement between them.

num_experts.source: INHERITED from laguna-tpu-opt-arch, received as bench-campaign/evidence/opt/em-succession.md at commit 64a3e599 section 4. Cited to that document per the citation rule; the sources it names were NOT opened or re-derived here. num_experts = 256 in the checkpoint config.
num_experts.note: Used only by the ILLUSTRATIVE uniform-expectation helper and by the model discriminator. Reachable from no decision path.

padded_block_rows.source: INHERITED from laguna-tpu-opt-arch, received as bench-campaign/evidence/opt/em-succession.md at commit 64a3e599 section 4. The routing block is 16 rows.
padded_block_rows.note: A CONFIGURATION FACT, not a measurement and not a model output. It is what makes dispersal a c1 phenomenon by construction: at c1 the block holds 1 real token and 15 padding rows, at c16 it holds 16 real tokens and NO padding rows, so padding-row dispersal raises E(1) and does not move E(16). Recorded here rather than left as a literal so that a different block size cannot silently keep the old padding-row count.

per_chip_hbm_bandwidth_gbytes_per_s.source: brief section C and optimization-design.md section 7 M6 -- the PER-CHIP row of the v7x table
per_chip_hbm_bandwidth_gbytes_per_s.note: Cite the row, not the value. This is per chip. The per-device figure is half of it and pairing the two bases is the fault M6 leg 2 exists to catch.

per_chip_dense_bf16_tflops.source: brief section C and optimization-design.md section 7 M6 -- the PER-CHIP row of the v7x table
per_chip_dense_bf16_tflops.note: Per chip. Per device is half.

devices_per_chip.source: brief section C: a v7x chip is two chiplets, which is two TensorCores, which is two JAX devices. The runtime device is the chiplet.
devices_per_chip.note: The device count is twice the chip count. Never derive a chip count from the startup banner's chip-count field: it reports devices.

max_tensor_parallel_size.source: brief section C: TP=16 is prohibited; TP=8 is 4 chips and is the ceiling because num_key_value_heads is 8

ridge_relative_tolerance.source: NOT A DESIGNED THRESHOLD. Floating-point equality epsilon for recomputing the ridge point from the pinned pair.
ridge_relative_tolerance.note: An inconsistent pairing moves the ridge by a factor of two, so no measurement-derived tolerance is needed to separate it from a rounding difference.

idle_definition.source: architect ruling, via brief section E6
idle_definition.note: STRICT: a gap on the device timeline with no kernel executing AND no DMA in flight. The thresholds below stand because they stand on the strict definition. Do not loosen it.

f_host_holds_at_or_above.source: architect judgement, via brief section E6 Rule 1
f_host_holds_at_or_above.note: f_host = I_strict / S, a fraction. A threshold expressed in the units of the thing being changed is not a threshold.

f_host_refuted_at_or_below.source: architect judgement, via brief section E6 Rule 1
f_host_refuted_at_or_below.note: Between the two bounds is MIXED, a defined first-class branch, never resolved into the nearer extreme.

e_dec_byte_bound_ratio.source: architect judgement, via brief section E6 Rule 2
e_dec_byte_bound_ratio.note: Basis recorded because a reader is entitled to weigh it: 0.85 is judgement, not derived from a measurement. What is principled is the ratio-to-reference form, not the number.

e_dec_efficiency_deficit_ratio.source: architect judgement, via brief section E6 Rule 2
e_dec_efficiency_deficit_ratio.note: Same basis as 0.85. A revision to either costs a parameter, by design.

e_ref_plausibility_floor.source: architect, via brief section E6 Rule 2
e_ref_plausibility_floor.note: If the measured reference efficiency comes back below this, Rule 2 is VOID rather than applied, and that is itself the finding.

reference_step_ms.note: REFERENCE ONLY. Not used in any verdict in this package. S is measured, and the decision is taken on the fraction I/S.

closure_residual_threshold.source: brief section E6a: 'No threshold is attached to this and you must not invent one. Emit the number.'
closure_residual_threshold.note: Held here as an explicit absence so that a future reader can see the gap was ruled, not overlooked.

bucket_overlap_threshold.note: Overlap is reported, not judged. Closure is necessary and not sufficient: overlapping buckets can sum to S while describing the step wrongly.
